supporting_observations.claim: The repeated HTTPS proxy connections attributed by endpoint telemetry to dgupdate.exe went to update.datagrid-analytics.co, whereas the approved updater domain in the supplied inventory is update.datagrid-analytics.com. The observed contacts recur at roughly five-minute intervals.

dgupdate.exe ran from Raj Iyer's AppData\Roaming\DataGrid directory, rather than the approved DataGrid installation directory specified in the inventory. Endpoint records associate this process with connections through the proxy.

The kim.ortega administrator account obtained Kerberos tickets from 10.20.10.22 for FILE-LV-01, followed by a logon to FILE-LV-01 from that same IP. The evidence identifies 10.20.10.22 as WS-RIYER-01, while the supplied inventory says remote administration is only performed from WS-KORTEGA-01.

An unapproved Dropbox client is present and launched on WS-RIYER-01; a later attempt to connect to desktop.dropbox.com was denied by the proxy. These records do not establish that any data was uploaded.

Raj Iyer's medium-integrity command prompt launched a SQL Server database-backup command and WMIC process enumeration. These actions add context but, by themselves, do not establish malicious intent or successful data collection.

known_telemetry_limitations: Proxy and network records show traffic through the explicit proxy; they do not provide the TLS payload for the repeated updater connections.
The supplied records do not include a hash, signature-validation result, or file provenance for dgupdate.exe.
The Dropbox connection attempt was denied; the evidence does not show whether the client had previously transferred data or whether other file-sharing channels were used.
The supplied time window and records may not represent all activity on the host or associated accounts.
claims_not_established: The evidence does not establish what data, if any, was sent to the updater domain or whether the domain served malicious content.
The evidence does not establish how dgupdate.exe was installed or whether it is malware, despite its unexpected location and domain mismatch.
The evidence does not establish whether the administrator credentials were compromised or whether there is an authorized explanation for their use from WS-RIYER-01.
The evidence does not establish that the database-backup command completed or that any database data left the workstation.
additional_evidence_needed: Acquire and preserve dgupdate.exe and related DataGrid files; collect hashes, signature and reputation results, and execution/download provenance.
Obtain proxy TLS inspection details, DNS and certificate data for update.datagrid-analytics.co, and any available server-side or endpoint evidence of transferred content.

Investigate the kim.ortega authentication: confirm the administrator's activity and authorization, review authentication and file-server access logs, and assess the credential for possible compromise.
Review Dropbox installation history, configuration, sync state, and any available proxy or endpoint records for prior or attempted transfers.
Collect relevant endpoint process, file, persistence, and network telemetry outside the supplied window to determine the scope and origin of the activity.
